name: PEN conductor mark
summary: A mark identifying a combined protective and neutral conductor, as used in TN-C sections of a supply.
description: The PEN mark identifies one conductor that performs both the protective and neutral functions. It appears in TN-C and TN-C-S arrangements, typically between the supply transformer and the main switchboard, where the PEN is later separated into N and PE at a defined point.

A PEN conductor must not be switched or isolated on its own, and once separated into N and PE the two must not be rejoined downstream. A drawing that shows a PEN mark should therefore also show the separation point clearly. The mark says nothing about minimum conductor size, which local wiring rules set for PEN conductors.
readingNotes: Find the point where the PEN is split into N and PE.
Check that no switching device opens the PEN conductor alone.
drawingChecklist: Show the PEN to N and PE separation point.
Avoid single-pole switching of the PEN.
Confirm PEN sizing against the applicable wiring rules.
distinction: A PEN conductor combines N and PE functions; a neutral mark shows a conductor that has no protective role.
